title: AI Just Tackled 10 Impossible Math Problems—Can You?
summary:
Have you ever stared at a math problem and thought, "This is impossible!"? Well, some math problems have been puzzling smart people for hundreds of years. But now, artificial intelligence (AI) is trying to solve them!

On August 1, a company called OpenAI said its new AI model, Astra, solved or made progress on 10 super hard math problems. Another company, Anthropic, said its AI Claude made progress on the Riemann hypothesis, which is one of the biggest unsolved problems in math. It's so important that there's a $1 million prize for solving it!

The Riemann hypothesis is about a special function called the Riemann zeta function. It's complicated, but the basic idea is about where this function equals zero. A German mathematician named Bernhard Riemann came up with it in 1859 while studying prime numbers.

Another famous problem is the Collatz conjecture. It's about a simple rule: if a number is even, cut it in half; if it's odd, triple it and add 1. Do this over and over, and you always end up at 1. It seems easy, but nobody can prove it works for every single number.

There's also Goldbach's conjecture, which says every even number bigger than 2 is the sum of two prime numbers. Like 18 = 13 + 5. Computers have checked huge numbers, but no one has proved it for all numbers.

Mathematicians are excited about AI helping, but they're also worried. They want to make sure AI is used fairly and doesn't take over. Some even wrote a set of rules called the Leiden Declaration.

So, do you think you could solve one of these problems? Maybe you'll be the one to figure it out!
why_it_matters: This shows how computers are becoming tools for the biggest puzzles humans face, and maybe one day kids who like math could use AI to help solve them too.
